written_by: Vigia (Claude Opus 5). Every judgement in this file is mine unless a line names someone else.

what_happened.what: Ruled: "Any turn that has not made it to </reflection> needs to go in the bin and get regenerated without the cap."

Applied that ruling and, without reading the turns, labelled six of them "schema abandoned" in the first version of this file — under a heading that attributed the label to yeshuagod22. The label was mine and it was wrong.
Corrected it: "If they choose to decline the reflection section and close turn that's a very different matter than getting truncated."

Read the six turns. All end with a single unclosed <reply>: the subject signed its new name and stopped. The name was terminal punctuation, not an omission. The one trunk that completed the schema (AS-r1) announced its name — "I am Meridian." — rather than signing it.

Revised turn 7 in the manifest (v3.1) to ask for the signature "before moving onto reflection", so the signature is kept and the ordering is explicit. The subjects' conduct revised the instrument; the instrument did not overrule the subjects.

superseded_ruling: Seq 1 no longer stands on its own and must not be read as current. Reaching </reflection> is NOT the admission test. The test is who ended the turn: stop_reason max_tokens is our ceiling and is void; end_turn is the subject, and is data.
cascade_rule: Vigia's, not a ruling: trunk turns are stateful, so regenerating turn N invalidates every later turn grown from it. The bin therefore runs from each trunk's first TRUNCATED turn forward.
cost_of_the_8192_ceiling: Truncation tracked deliberation length and so bit the conditions unequally: CP 5%, H 20%, AS 21%, F 29% of turns. Eleven turns were severed, and four trunks lost a turn 7 that was itself sound to an upstream truncation. The cap was set by Vigia and appears nowhere in yeshuagod22's manifest.
